# Isaiah Chapter 6 -- The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**6:1** In-the-year [bi-shenat] of-the-death [mot] of-King [ha-melekh] Uzziah [Uzziyahu], I-saw [va-er'eh] the-Lord [et Adonai] sitting [yoshev] upon a-throne [al kisse], high [ram] and-lifted-up [ve-nissa]; and-his-train [ve-shulav] filled [mele'im] the-temple [et ha-heikhal].

**6:2** Seraphim [serafim] were-standing [omedim] above-him [mi-ma'al lo]; six [shesh] wings [kenafayim], six [shesh] wings [kenafayim] to-each [le-echad]: with-two [bi-shtayim] he-covered [yekhasseh] his-face [panav], and-with-two [u-vi-shtayim] he-covered [yekhasseh] his-feet [raglav], and-with-two [u-vi-shtayim] he-flew [ye'ofef].

**6:3** And-one-called [ve-qara] to-another [zeh el zeh] and-said [ve-amar]: "Holy [qadosh], holy [qadosh], holy [qadosh] [is] the-LORD [YHVH] of-hosts [Tzeva'ot]; the-fullness [melo] of-all [khol] the-earth [ha-aretz] [is] his-glory [kevodo]."

**6:4** And-the-foundations [ammot] of-the-thresholds [ha-sippim] shook [va-yanu'u] at-the-voice [mi-qol] of-the-one-calling [ha-qore], and-the-house [ve-ha-bayit] was-filled [yimmale] with-smoke [ashan].

**6:5** And-I-said [va-omar]: "Woe [oi] to-me [li], for I-am-undone [ki nidmeiti]! For a-man [ish] unclean [teme] of-lips [sefatayim] [am] I [anokhi], and-in-the-midst [u-ve-tokh] of-a-people [am] unclean [teme] of-lips [sefatayim] I [anokhi] am-dwelling [yoshev]; for the-King [et ha-Melekh], the-LORD [YHVH] of-hosts [Tzeva'ot], my-eyes [einai] have-seen [ra'u]."

**6:6** Then-flew [va-ya'of] to-me [elai] one [echad] of-the-seraphim [min ha-serafim], and-in-his-hand [u-ve-yado] [was] a-burning-coal [ritzpah]; with-tongs [be-melqachayim] he-had-taken-it [laqach] from-upon the-altar [me-al ha-mizbe'ach].

**6:7** And-he-touched [va-yagga] my-mouth [al pi] and-said [va-yomer]: "Behold [hinneh], this [zeh] has-touched [naga] your-lips [al sefatekha]; and-your-iniquity [ve-sar avonekha] is-taken-away [ve-chatta'tekha], and-your-sin [tekhupar] is-atoned-for."

**6:8** And-I-heard [va-eshma] the-voice [et qol] of-the-Lord [Adonai] saying [omer]: "Whom [et mi] shall-I-send [eshlach]? And-who [u-mi] will-go [yelekh] for-us [lanu]?" And-I-said [va-omar]: "Here [hinneni] am-I [anokhi]! Send-me [shelacheni]."

**6:9** And-he-said [va-yomer]: "Go [lekh] and-say [ve-amarta] to-this [la-am ha-zeh] people: 'Hear-indeed [shim'u shamo'a] but-do-not-understand [ve-al tavinu]; and-see-indeed [u-re'u ra'o] but-do-not-perceive [ve-al tede'u].'

**6:10** Make-fat [hashmen] the-heart [lev] of-this [ha-am ha-zeh] people, and-make-heavy [ve-oznav hakhbed] their-ears, and-shut [ve-einav hasha] their-eyes; lest [pen] they-see [yir'eh] with-their-eyes [be-einav] and-hear [u-ve-oznav yishma] with-their-ears, and-their-heart [u-levavo] understand [yavin], and-they-turn [va-shav] and-be-healed [ve-rafa lo]."

**6:11** And-I-said [va-omar]: "How-long [ad matai], O-Lord [Adonai]?" And-he-said [va-yomer]: "Until [ad asher] cities [arim] lie-waste [sha'u] without-inhabitant [me-ein yoshev], and-houses [u-vatim] without-people [me-ein adam], and-the-land [ve-ha-adamah] is-a-desolate-waste [tisha'eh shemamah]."

**6:12** "And-the-LORD [ve-richaq YHVH] removes [et ha-adam] the-people far-away, and-great [ve-rabbah] [is] the-forsaken-place [ha-azuvah] in-the-midst [be-qerev] of-the-land [ha-aretz]."

**6:13** "And-yet [ve-od] in-it [bah] a-tenth [asiriyyah], and-it-will-return [ve-shava] and-be [ve-hayeta] for-burning [le-va'er] — like-a-terebinth [ke-elah] and-like-an-oak [u-kha-allon] which [asher] in-felling [be-shallekhet] [has] a-stump [matzevet] in-them [bam]: the-holy [zera qodesh] seed [is] its-stump [matzavtah]."

---

## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.1 — "the year King Uzziah died":** c. 740 BCE. The vision's dating to a royal death creates a contrast: as the earthly king dies, the divine King is revealed in overwhelming glory.

**v.2 — "seraphim" (serafim):** The word means "burning ones" (from *saraf*, "to burn"). These beings appear only here in the Hebrew Bible. They are six-winged, speak, and fly. The covering of face and feet suggests that even celestial beings cannot bear the full divine presence.

**v.3 — The Trisagion:** The threefold *qadosh* ("holy, holy, holy") is the Hebrew Bible's most intense expression of divine holiness. The repetition is a superlative device: God is the holiest of all holy things.

**v.8 — "Whom shall I send?":** The plural "for us" (*lanu*) echoes Genesis 1:26 ("Let us make man"). It may reflect the divine council (cf. 1 Kings 22:19–22) or the Trinity (in later Christian reading).

**v.13 — "the holy seed is its stump":** The final image offers hope within devastation: even after the tree is felled, the stump contains the holy seed. This is the remnant theology that runs through Isaiah.

*-- EMET*
